title: Stock Exchange Matching Engine
summary: An exchange matches buy and sell orders fairly and very fast, millions per second with microsecond latency. The trick is determinism. Every order passes risk checks, then a sequencer gives it one global position in a journal, and a single-threaded matching engine replays that journal in order. Any replica fed the same journal reaches exactly the same order book, which makes failover and audits possible.

walkthrough.title: Submit an order
walkthrough.text: A broker sends a FIX NewOrderSingle: buy 500 ACME limit $101.20. It arrives at an order gateway in the exchange's co-location data centre.

walkthrough.title: Pre-trade risk checks
walkthrough.text: The gateway checks the member's credit limit, price bands (no buying at 10× the last price), maximum order size, and kill-switch status in a few microseconds.

walkthrough.title: Sequence and journal
walkthrough.text: The sequencer gives the order the next global sequence number and writes it to a replicated journal. This one ordering is the official history of the market.

walkthrough.title: Match by price-time priority
walkthrough.text: The single-threaded matching engine applies the order to the ACME book. It fills against the best-priced resting sells, and earlier orders at the same price go first. The rest rests on the book.

walkthrough.title: Execution reports
walkthrough.text: Both sides get execution reports (filled 300 @ 101.18, 200 resting) back through the sequencer and gateway.

walkthrough.title: Publish market data
walkthrough.text: Every trade and book change goes out on a multicast feed to all subscribers at the same moment, so nobody sees prices earlier than anyone else.

walkthrough.title: Clear and settle
walkthrough.text: Trades go to the clearing house, which becomes the counterparty to both sides (novation), nets positions, and settles cash and shares on T+1.

data.label: Brokers & Traders
responsibilities: Send orders on behalf of clients and their own trading.
Track their open orders from execution reports.
Run their own risk controls before orders leave the firm.

failureModes.impact: Thousands of erroneous orders in seconds (Knight Capital lost $440M in 45 minutes).
failureModes.mitigation: Exchange-side kill switches and per-member order-rate and position limits.

data.label: Order Gateway & Risk
responsibilities: Authenticates member sessions and normalises protocols.
Runs pre-trade risk checks without adding much latency.
Returns execution reports to the right session.

failureModes.mitigation: Equal cable lengths and identical hardware for every member.

failureModes.impact: A member trades beyond its collateral.
failureModes.mitigation: Limits updated intraday from clearing; reject by default when unknown.

data.label: Sequencer & Journal
responsibilities: Puts every event into one global order.
Persists and replicates the journal before matching acts on it.
Lets any replica rebuild the exact market state by replay.

failureModes.impact: Trading halts until a new one takes over.
failureModes.mitigation: Hot standby consuming the same journal; deterministic takeover in milliseconds.
Gap detection with retransmission; checksums on book state.

data.label: Matching Engine

input.name: Sequenced events
input.type: New / cancel / replace in sequence order

responsibilities: Matches by price, then time: best price first, earliest first at the same price.
Is deterministic: the same input sequence always gives the same output.
Runs auctions at open and close and enforces halts and circuit breakers.

failureModes.mitigation: No allocation on the hot path, pinned CPU cores, kernel bypass networking.

failureModes.impact: Erroneous trades far from fair value.
failureModes.mitigation: Limit-up/limit-down bands, volatility halts, and erroneous-trade rules.

data.label: Market Data Feed
responsibilities: Publishes every order-book change to all subscribers at once.
Provides snapshot and retransmit services for recovery.
Supplies the official prices used by indices and regulators.

failureModes.impact: Its view of the book is wrong.
failureModes.mitigation: Sequence numbers, A/B redundant feeds, and gap retransmission.
Capacity headroom for peak bursts; latency monitoring per packet.

data.label: Clearing & Settlement

output.name: Settlement
output.type: Net obligations; shares and cash move on T+1

responsibilities: Becomes buyer to every seller and seller to every buyer (novation).
Nets each member's trades into one obligation per security.
Collects margin so one member's default cannot cascade.

failureModes.mitigation: Margin, a default fund, and auctioning the defaulter's positions.
Real-time drop copies and end-of-day reconciliation.
